clue.text: Drink in brother's bar, after cutting back

indicators.note: cutting trims a word short, here docking the tail of bar
back tells the solver to read the joined letters from right to left

blocks.note: BRO is short for brother, plus the possessive S
taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone drinking at their brother's pub after a spell of cutting down.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR loses its R to give BA; BROS plus BA, read backwards, gives ABSORB.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink in, like a sponge, is to soak up or take in, which is absorbing.

clue.text: Taking lid off bottle, pour forth drink

indicators.note: the lid is the top of a bottle, so only its first letter is taken

blocks.note: the top letter of bottle
to ooze is to flow or seep out

explanation.surface: Someone uncorks a bottle and pours out a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is the informal word for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Blur face, but so grotesquely

indicators.note: something grotesque is distorted out of its natural shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An image of a face distorted into something grotesque and blurred.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to make unclear or obscure, so it is to blur.

clue.text: Little room in English county with hi-tech

blocks.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, a county north of London
joins the two pieces
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A small modern flat in the English shires fitted with gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British term for a single rented room used for both living and sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single small rented room serving as bedroom and living space.

clue.text: Pointer tossing rubbish around playfully at first

indicators.note: rubbish as an adjective means poor or worthless, so the word before it is to be knocked into a new shape
at first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it
around means the jumbled letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
first letter of playfully

explanation.surface: Someone playfully tossing rubbish about in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing looks like the anagram verb, but it is the fodder; rubbish is the signal, and P goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost is a post that points the way, so it is a pointer.

clue.text: Digger initially going in faster, as annual repairs concerning underground line?

indicators.note: initially points to just the first letter of digger
going in means the single letter enters the following set of letters
repairs as a verb means fixes, putting the letters together in a new working order

blocks.note: first letter of digger
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A digger working faster to finish annual roadworks above an Underground railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Underground line suggests the London Tube, but here it is a crack running beneath the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The San Andreas Fault is a geological fracture in California, literally a line running below the ground.

clue.text: Primate taking lunch in Merlot, say?

indicators.note: taking means holding something inside, so the wine takes in the meal
in completes the picture of one piece being placed within the other

blocks.note: Merlot is an example of a grape variety
to lunch is to eat

explanation.surface: A primate drinking red wine over lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Great apes, such as gorillas and chimpanzees, are a group of primates.

clue.text: Musician and cake decorator?

blocks.note: first meaning: a player of the bagpipes
second meaning: one who pipes icing onto a cake

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented sense: someone who pipes icing.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays pipes, and anyone squeezing icing from a nozzle pipes it, so the word fits both.

clue.text: Restaurant worker in battle that is grasped by both hands

indicators.note: grasped by means held within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the Somme was a major First World War battle
L and R stand for left and right
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A waiter caught up in a war, clutched by both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is the wine waiter employed in a restaurant.

clue.text: Study poem rejected by poet, trusted friend

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the poem title is turned around

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study
If is Kipling's famous poem
Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet

explanation.surface: A poet turning down a poem he studied, sharing his doubts with a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidante is a person one trusts with private matters.

clue.text: Use force to remove shoe

blocks.note: first meaning: to draw out by pressure, as water from a well
second meaning: a light flat shoe

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests wrenching a shoe off; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump water out is to force it out, and a pump is a light slip-on shoe.

clue.text: Again transfer rule-breaking fool

indicators.note: breaking means split open, so the rule word is parted to let the other word in

blocks.note: to reign is to rule
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool caught breaking the rules is moved on again.
explanation.walkthrough: Rule-breaking reads as one adjective, but it splits into the rule word and the breaking signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign is to allocate or transfer something a second time.

clue.text: Reversal of routine important for country

indicators.note: Reversal of plainly asks for the next word to be read backwards

blocks.note: a rut is a dull routine
key means important

explanation.surface: Breaking out of a dull routine matters for a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is a country spanning south-east Europe and western Asia.

clue.text: Hit on the turn, a soldier

indicators.note: on the turn means turning round, so the hit word is read backwards

blocks.note: a rap is a sharp blow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier is struck as he turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Para is short for paratrooper, a parachute soldier.

clue.text: A fine period at hospital — result!

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a term is a period of time
taken as written
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A good spell in hospital, and a successful outcome to cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the consequence or result following an event.

clue.text: Remains hanging around auberge in France, perhaps

indicators.note: hanging around means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a relic is something that remains from the past
an auberge is a French inn, so a pub

explanation.surface: Remains of the past lingering around a French country inn.
explanation.definitionFit: France is an example of a republic, a state with an elected head rather than a monarch.

clue.text: Lovely, nasty surprise

blocks.note: first meaning, as a noun: a very attractive woman
second meaning: a shocking, unwelcome piece of news

explanation.walkthrough: Lovely reads as an adjective but is the noun for a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombshell is slang for a stunning woman and also for a shattering, unexpected revelation.

clue.text: Throw black rock like that into container

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so one piece is put within the container word

blocks.note: jet is a hard black mineral used in jewellery
a tin is a container
so means in that way

explanation.surface: An instruction to toss a black stone into a bin.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard.

clue.text: Create broadcast on film, and so on

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a broadcast about a film.
explanation.walkthrough: On means the film's two letters sit beside the rearranged letters; here they land in the middle of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for and the rest, used to mean and so on.

clue.text: Red stains by one's ears?

indicators.note: judged by one's ears means going on what is heard rather than written

blocks.note: marks are stains

explanation.surface: Red stains near someone's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: Red looks like the colour of the stains; it is a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx, founder of communism, is the archetypal Red.

clue.text: Where entertainment had dismissing opener, not cricket!

indicators.note: dismissing the opener sends the first one away, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a funfair is a place where fun is had

explanation.surface: A cricket match where the opening batsman was given out unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: Not cricket is a British idiom for unsporting, and dismissing an opener is cricket talk borrowed for the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not cricket means it is unsporting or unjust.

clue.text: Horror film's introduction, okay

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of film
right means okay

explanation.surface: Approval of a horror film's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Horror film reads as a genre, but horror is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden feeling of fear, a synonym for horror.

clue.text: Crude measure of old

blocks.note: first meaning: coarse or vulgar
second meaning: an old counting unit of twelve dozen

explanation.definitionFit: Gross means coarse or vulgar, and a gross is 144, a traditional quantity now seldom used.

clue.text: Over bit of fish I cast

blocks.note: a fin is part of a fish
taken as written
to shed is to cast off

explanation.surface: An angler complaining about a part of a fish he cast.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast looks like an anagram signal, but it is the synonym for shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over has ended, so it is finished.

clue.text: Bug turning up in silo, certainly

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the next words of the clue
in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A pest turning up in a grain silo, without doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium, and a bug is the everyday word for a germ.

clue.text: Starter of organic root vegetable turned over in sauce

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter
turned over means flipped, so the joined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: first letter of organic
a yam is a starchy tuber

explanation.surface: An organic root vegetable dish served in a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter looks like a first course, which suits the kitchen picture, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is short for mayonnaise, a cold sauce.

clue.text: Long canine used, sago roughly cut by fang, regularly

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
second and fourth letters of fang

explanation.definitionFit: Sausage dog is the informal name for a dachshund, a dog with a long body.

clue.text: Old crack in wood?

blocks.note: first meaning: a stale joke told too often
second meaning: timber from a particular tree

explanation.walkthrough: Crack reads as a split in timber, but it means a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a joke heard too many times, and chestnut is also a hardwood.

clue.text: During attack, foreign article put down again

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a raid is an attack
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.definitionFit: To relay a floor or cable is to lay it down a second time.
